decision.title: The last streamed shapes: accumulators, xsl:fork and the principal result while streaming (packet 7.6e)

body.p: , after , , , , , , . Replaces 's and 's "accumulators computed while streaming are not done" and their rule that a stylesheet reading an accumulator streams nothing.

item.p: Accumulators while streaming (XSLT 4.0, 18.2.9, 19.3, 19.4; glossary ): STREAM with OPENS_DOCUMENT gets sxml_ir_stream_accumulators, four functions of the unit (src/xslt_accumulator.c): stream-initial-N($root), the initial values of the accumulators applicable to the document (19.2: use-accumulators of xsl:source-document, or of the initial mode for a streamed principal source; those declared streamable), and stream-start-0, stream-end-0 and stream-descend-0 ($node, $value, $number), start-K, end-K and the new descend-K (build-K's traversal of one subtree) of accumulator $number. Each event a STREAM task takes calls them before the task goes on (the task suspends and resumes, ): an element's start in a shallow window of its own, which is the window the body then sees, its end, a leaf's start and end, the document's end; skipped content is taken event by event; a full window (a selected subtree, a grounding stream) gets its subtree's values from descend-K at once. Values are maps from accumulator numbers, kept per depth for the nodes the windows hold now (memory bounded by the depth and the windows, as before).

Reading them: fn:accumulator-before and -after ask the new row accumulator-streamed($number, $node, $id, $after) first when some accumulator is declared streamable; it finds the node among the values the running streamed documents keep (sxml_evaluator_stream_find_ accumulator_values, src/evaluator_internal.h) and otherwise leaves the node to accumulator-values (trees, unchanged). XTDE3362 for an accumulator the document does not apply; XTSE3430 (dynamic) for fn:accumulator-after of a node whose end has not been read.

Order and errors: the values of one node are computed accumulator by accumulator; a rule that reads a value of the same node not computed yet makes its accumulator wait for a later round (the row raises, the STREAM catches it), and a round without progress raises XTDE3400. A rule's error is caught and kept; reads of the values it left out raise it (19.5: errors surface when a value is asked for), so values computed before it stay readable.

When: a stylesheet that reads accumulators now streams unless an accumulator declared streamable has an end rule with capture="yes" (19.9: its end event would need the node's subtree) or is not guaranteed-streamable (new sxml_xslt_assess_accumulators, 7.6a's check of 18.2.9; with the fallback option of 19.10 such an accumulator compiles, and its rules would read a shallow window); then the document is grounded, as before. sxml_xslt_reads_accumulators (now with an allocator and name pool, for sxml_xslt_stylesheet_streams_source too) means that; the comments of xslt.h say so (no interface change).

Post-descent: an instruction after the stream point of a streamed body is assessed as following a consuming one (new field sxml_xslt_sweep_query.follows_consuming; 19.8.9.1 rule 8), so fn:accumulator-after of the node there is motionless and the body streams.

xsl:fork (16.1, 18.3; glossary ): in the body of a streamed xsl:source-document (document focus, also inside literal result elements and xsl:sequence without select, which now wrap their content), an xsl:fork whose children are xsl:sequence (and xsl:fallback) and that reads the document's content gets one pass per prong: each prong is planned as a streamed body of its own and lowered to a STREAM with OPENS_DOCUMENT over the same href, the values concatenated in prong order. The document is so parsed once per prong (and once for the body around the fork), each pass in bounded memory; a processor may evaluate the prongs in any way that gives their results (18.3), and the resolver is asked again for each pass. A fork some prong of which does not stream, or with xsl:for-each-group, is grounded as before.

The principal result as it is made (2.4, 26.1; glossary , ): a transformation that streams its principal source with SERIALIZED delivery, a tree built (build-tree yes, a method given that builds one, or no method; 26.1), no item-separator and no xsl:result-document instruction lowers its main function as DOCUMENT with the new construction flag PRINCIPAL_RESULT over the whole body (the invocation then delivers into it, ; the built principal result now takes the same shape without the flag). That DOCUMENT builds into the result writer's principal stream (environment field principal_result_builder) and makes no tree. Without build-tree and method, a first item that is a map, an array or a JNode makes the method json (26.1.2): the construction then keeps the raw value (environment field principal_result_is_raw), the stream, which has written nothing, is dropped, and the raw result is delivered as before. The stream chooses the method from the first evidence (26.1.2) and the output definition: for the xml method with no indent, no canonical form, no doctype and standalone omitted, a streamed serialization writes each event as it arrives (one small tree per open element, for the start tag's namespaces; its parent's bindings are inherited unless the element binds the prefix itself); for any other method the events build the tree, which is serialized at the end as before. The serializer is unchanged: start tags, text, comments and processing instructions go through the XML method's own writer functions (src/serialize_xml.c), refactored out of its tree walk.

Measured (sxml transform, release, 95.6 MB document, 904,745 records; peak resident set): the streamed identity (on-no-match shallow-copy) 525 MB before, 134 MB after, output identical; an accumulator counting the records with accumulator-before and -after more than 4.1 GB before (stopped at 207 s), 135 MB after; a for-each over the hot records 134 MB before and after. What is left is the input, which the CLI holds whole. evaluator_stream_test: the identity of a 2.4 MB document streams with a peak of 189 KB of allocator memory. XT40 (release, case by case): 12,031 to 12,048 passed, none lost (the gains include other packets' commits in between).

Not done: capture="yes" end rules while streaming; an accumulator value of a window node no entry holds any more (a streamed node kept past its body) falls back to the tree of its window. xsl:merge with streamed inputs (15.3) needs several streamed documents read in step, one cursor each with the merge keys of its current item, and a part that interleaves them; that is a new evaluator part, not a shape of STREAM, and stays for a packet of its own (merge sources are grounded, as before). Bytes delivered incrementally to the parser: the planned interface is an additive resource form in processor.h, SXML_RESOURCE_FORM_BYTE_READER, a reader whose read operation fills a buffer the parser lends and reports the end, with release as for BYTES; the incremental parse (, ) then decodes and checks the input a window at a time, as segments, instead of at its creation, and the CLI serves the input file through it. The parser change is in src/xml.c, src/xml_segment.c and src/xml_encoding.c, which another packet (perf-3) is changing now, so neither the form nor the parser change is made here; the header is unchanged.
